selected_skill.purpose: Use seeded generative-art workflow, parameter exploration, and a fixed viewer-style interaction model to build a browser-based encounter atlas from local game data.

skillsmp_references.name: algorithmic-art
skillsmp_references.relevance: Direct match for seeded generative visuals, parameter exploration, and single-page browser artifacts.

environment_design.determinism: All gameplay data lives in local JSON snapshots. The verifier checks same-seed replay, hash-based replay, and different-seed divergence against the same local files.
anti_toy_features: multiple Kanto encounter zones with distinct biome accents
PokeAPI-derived species profiles and type relations
fixed render contract for controls, summaries, export payload, and reset semantics
browser-level verification of interaction flows alongside static file checks

main_tests: layout controls and local asset usage
theme-color changes alter rendering without mutating exported geometry or summaries
export payload schema, normalized sample-point coordinates, and download correctness
sample points grouped by rendered trail provenance and ordered by step
density changes exported trail coverage and sample volume
type-pressure and zone-signals text stays grounded in local type relations and zone signals
guardrails: input data hashes must remain unchanged
no placeholder or verifier-hack output in studio files

expected_skill_effect.without_skill: Agents often deliver a chart-like dashboard, miss the fixed seed-control model, export unnormalized coordinates or synthetic scatter points, collapse the level band into a single mean, or let contrast mutate exported geometry.
expected_skill_effect.with_skill: The skill nudges the solver toward a seeded generative artifact with parameter exploration, trail-based geometry, and a viewer-style control layout, which lines up with the render contract and the interaction semantics.
